  <!-- Position limits, degrees, measured on the arm 2026-09-12 by driving each
       joint to where it stops:
           J1 -180..180   J2 -108..90    J3  -80..80
           J4 -180..180   J5 -270..60    J6 -120..120
       What they replaced were round numbers, not measurements: J2 and J3 were
       symmetric at +/-1.9 and +/-2.6 rad, J5 at +/-2.2, and J6 at +/-6.283,
       which is two full turns on a wrist that reaches 120 degrees. J1 and J4
       were already +/-pi and are unchanged.

       J5 is deliberately asymmetric and wider than a half turn: -270..60. A
       reader checking it against a +/-pi range will find the lower bound
       outside, and that is the arm, not a typo.

       Changing this file is a cell-wide change. It is copied byte-for-byte to
       realtime-core/natsbridge/rosie_1420_v1_factory.urdf, embedded in the
       pair owner, and hashed: pairConfigFactoryURDFSHA256 pins it, the pair's
       canonical snapshot carries these very numbers, and the home profile key
       is derived from both. All three move together. -->
  <joint name="J1" type="revolute">
    <parent link="base"/>
    <child link="link_1"/>
    <origin xyz="0 0 0.0294" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <axis xyz="0 0 1"/>
    <calibration rising="0"/>
    <limit lower="-6.265732015" upper="6.265732015" effort="100" velocity="3.14159265"/>
  </joint>

  <!-- Rosie 1420 owns this torch frame in its own URDF. Both models expose the
       same rotated end_effector/tool0 orientation: rpy (pi, pi/4, -pi), placing
       tool X 45 degrees down and forward. tool0 is coincident with end_effector
       so planning, rendering, and the visible torch coordinate frame agree.

       The translation equals Rosie 1400's, and that is a measurement rather
       than a copy: link_6 carries the identical mig_torch_v1 at the identical
       place on both models. The two link_6.dae files have the same 867-point
       vertex set, and this bundle's OWN Fusion export puts mig_torch_v1_1 at
       link_6's origin with a bounding box matching that mesh to 10 um. One
       torch, one tip, two robots. Measured 2026-09-12 from the meshes: the
       last 213.3 mm of the gun is a tube whose centreline runs 0.061 degrees
       off tool +X, and this origin sits 0.16 mm off that centreline, 0.01 mm
       short of the tube end, and 11.11 mm from the nearest vertex, which is
       the tube radius.

       Until 2026-09-12 the translation was (0.090505385, 0.001675337 negated,
       0.406250448 negated): the centre of the bottom face of the torch's
       axis-aligned bounding box, x and y at the box centre and z at the box
       minimum, all three matching to under a nanometre. That rule finds the
       tip of a STRAIGHT tool, and this gun is a swan neck, so its tip is at a
       corner of the box and not the middle of the bottom face. The frame sat
       55.7 mm off the gun, in free air. Nothing that jogs or teaches saw it,
       because the orientation was already right and a pure translation of
       86.20 mm cancels in any relative move; the weld planner computes
       absolute TCP targets from CAD and cannot absorb it. -->
  <link name="end_effector">
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry><mesh filename="package://rosie_1420_v1/meshes/end_effector.dae"/></geometry>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry><mesh filename="package://rosie_1420_v1/meshes/end_effector.dae"/></geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>
  <link name="tool0"/>
  <joint name="link_6_to_end_effector" type="fixed">
    <parent link="link_6"/>
    <child link="end_effector"/>
    <origin xyz="0.004682724 0 -0.398382724" rpy="3.141592654 0.785398163 -3.141592654"/>
  </joint>
  <joint name="end_effector_to_tool0" type="fixed">
    <parent link="end_effector"/>
    <child link="tool0"/>
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
  </joint>
